articles.title: Staff killed and wounded in Russian strike on Kyiv’s science academy
articles.summary: Moscow’s jet-powered drones pummel Ukraine’s capital in switch to daytime attacks

blocks.text: Russia has hit the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv with a drone, killing at least one person in the latest daytime attack on Ukraine’s capital.
Flames tore through the historic building on Monday as people clambered out of first- and second-floor windows to escape, in dramatic scenes increasingly familiar in the heavily bombarded city.
At least one person was killed and three others were wounded, according to Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, who said the injured had been taken to hospital.
The 19th-century building stands close to the German embassy, the National Opera, St Volodymyr’s Cathedral and several government buildings.

Anatoliy Zagorodny, president of the national academy, said the blast struck while many staff members were inside. Standing outside the burning building, he said he did not know why Russia had targeted a leading centre of scientific research. “We are not connected with the military. This is an attack on science. It is terrorism,” he said.
He said he feared some of his colleagues could still be trapped inside the academy.

While the sciences building is a civilian scientific institution, it has longstanding ties to Ukraine’s defence sector. Among those injured in Monday’s strike was Volodymyr Horbulin, the academy’s first vice-president and a former high-ranking security official.
Another Russian drone struck a nearby private medical centre, killing at least one person.

Russian strikes over the past week involving missiles and increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones have hit apartment blocks, offices, warehouses and datacentres across the capital, killing and wounding civilians almost daily and giving Kyiv an increasingly frontline feel as it faces some of its most sustained bombardment since the early stages of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

The drone and missile campaign is designed to grind down public resilience and damage the economy. Monday’s double strike is likely to raise fresh concerns over Ukraine’s ability to protect even the most heavily guarded parts of the capital.
after newsletter promotion

The newer jet-powered drones fly faster and are harder to intercept than the older Shahed or Geran-2 models that were the backbone of Moscow’s air campaign. Ukraine is now racing to develop and manufacture interceptors capable of bringing them down.
Moscow has also changed its tactics, launching more attacks in daylight hours so that residents in major cities have to spend more of the day under air raid alerts.
Buildings hit during daytime strikes are often occupied because many Ukrainians work through drone alerts rather than spend hours in shelters.
Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, called on western countries to intensify their pressure on Russia.

“Every Russian terrorist attack is a loss of life that could have been prevented if pressure on Russia had finally become total,” he wrote on X on Monday. “The world must understand that terrorists will go further if they are not stopped here, in Ukraine. And we cannot turn a blind eye to such brutal strikes.”
Russia has signalled that its attacks on Ukraine could intensify and US-brokered efforts to end the war show little sign of progress.

“Ukraine will have to pay a price for the actions that have taken place in recent months,” the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, told reporters on Monday, referring to Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russian territory. “That is happening right now.”

articles.title: Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
articles.summary: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

image.caption: Catania lies in the foothills of Mount Etna, flights to the city are frequently disrupted by the active volcanoImage: Salvatore Allegra/Anadolu/IMAGO

blocks.text: Flight restrictions at Italy's Catania Aiport were extended on Monday, following disruptions to services over the weekend.
A thick ash cloud emanating from the nearby Mount Etna volcano has prompted authorities to halt flights.
What do we know about the disruption?
The Sicilian aiport's operator, SAC, said that all flight operations at the hub had been suspended until at least midnight local time (2200 GMT/UTC) on Monday night.
It said that where possible arrivals and departures were transferring to Sicily's other airports in Palermo and Comiso. Catania is Italy's fifth-busiest airport, and Sicily's largest hub.

blocks.caption: Catania airport said that where possible, flights were diverting to Sicily's other airports, Palermo or Comiso Image: Salvatore Allegra/Anadolu/IMAGO

blocks.text: SAC advised passengers to check the status of their flights prior to setting off for the airport.
The Mediterranean island is a popular holiday destination but travelers have faced frequent disruptions this summer because of eruptions and more commonly because of ash emanating from Etna.
Ash from the northeast crater of the mountain is being carried southward by the wind.
Italian Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) said the ash did not appear to indicate an imminent explosive phase.
What is Mount Etna?

Mount Etna is a roughly 3,400 meter (roughly 11,100 feet) stratovolcano on Sicily's eastern coast. Its precise height is ever changing, particularly amid periods of high activity when it can shed a few meters.
The city of Catania is located not far to the south.

blocks.caption: Despite the dangers, settling near volcanoes also has advantages like rich soil, hence Catania's success down the centuriesImage: Salvatore Allegra/Anadolu/IMAGO

blocks.text: Etna is one of the tallest active volcanoes in Europe and Italy's highest peak south of the Alps.

It's in an almost constant state of low-level activity and erupts in a more pronounced manner fairly frequently. It has caused disruptions at Catania airport several times this year, and in recent years.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the first volcanic activity took place at Etna about half a million years ago.
Both Roman and Greek mythology asserted that the god of blacksmithing — either Vulcan or Hephaestus — had his forge beneath Mount Etna.

articles.title: Queensland anti-corruption commission investigated just 20 of more than 6,000 complaints in a year
articles.summary:
Statistics showed there is ‘almost no chance’ a complaint made against a government department like the police would be investigated independently, expert says

  • Get our

blocks.text: Queensland’s anti-corruption commission has investigated just 20 of more than 6,000 complaints of suspected corruption in the past year, as the state government comes under renewed pressure to implement a years-late recommendation to end the practice of police investigating police.
The statistic was revealed in Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission’s annual report, tabled in state parliament on Friday afternoon.
It revealed the CCC assessed 6,198 corruption complaints in 2025-26. It referred 4,244 back to the agency concerned, including the police, local government and public service departments.
University of the Sunshine Coast criminology professor Tim Prenzler said the statistics showed the state was still operating a “discredited” approach, “facilitating misconduct through impunity”.
Prenzler was one of the key experts who advised the landmark 2022 commission of inquiry into police responses to domestic violence.

The inquiry considered numerous cases of conflicts of interest and lack of independence in police investigations of its officers. In one case, a police officer was even tasked with investigating their own actions.

Subsequent reporting by the Guardian has also revealed allegations by former police officers that the QPS covered up its own failures prior to domestic and family violence deaths and that in other cases policing failures were never properly investigated.

It recommended creating a new independent organisation – known as a police integrity unit – to investigate all complaints against police by May 2024, as one of its “four highest-priority recommendations”.
Both parties of government backed the recommendation, but progress has stalled.
Prenzler said the statistics showed that there was “almost no chance” a complaint made against a government department like the police would be investigated independently.

“From the outside, the CCC looks like a powerful independent agency that will thoroughly investigate all allegations and suspicions of public sector misconduct, protect parties, and provide justice,” he said.
“In reality, complainants and whistleblowers will have their expectations dashed as their matter is referred back to the agency involved and they will be doubly traumatised by the process.”
He said there was no rational justification for delaying the recommendation.
“Setting up the police integrity unit must be amongst the easiest things a government could do.”
after newsletter promotion
The state’s police minister, Dan Purdie, said police “have got really robust systems when it comes to complaints about police”.
“All of those matters are overseen by the CCC. That’s been the case for a long time, and they review all of those matters,” he said.
The CCC assessed 6,198 complaints in 2025-26.

It retained 20 for its own investigation. It referred 4,244 to the “appropriate agency’”, with 46 referred subject to CCC monitoring, 375 with a requirement for advice on its outcome, and 3,823 referred without any oversight.
It also assessed 1,934 complaints as “requiring no further action”.
Asked if the unit would be established by the 2028 state election, Purdie referred the question to the attorney general.
Unlike New South Wales’ Icac, the CCC is also responsible for investigating crimes like murder and rape that don’t involve corruption.
The CCC held 16 days of corruption hearings in 2025-26 but more than 100 days of crime hearings, its annual report revealed.
The annual report revealed the number of corruption complaints has been steadily increasing, up about 47% in the last four years.

articles.title: Further interest rate hikes could ‘devastate’ property market without easing unaffordability
articles.summary:
With RBA predicted to lift cash rate for fourth time this year on Tuesday, experts warn a fifth – or even sixth – rise would be ‘overkill’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Two or even three more Reserve Bank interest rate hikes would be “devastating” for the property market but still leave housing more unaffordable than ever as higher borrowing costs trump lower prices, experts say.

The RBA’s monetary policy board is widely expected on Tuesday afternoon to announce an increase in its cash rate to 4.6%, from 4.35%, in a decision that will add another $100 to the monthly mortgage interest bill on a $700,000 loan.
A number of analysts are tipping a further interest rate rise – the fifth this year – on Melbourne Cup day. Financial markets are even pricing in a 60% chance of a sixth rate increase by mid-2027.

As petrol prices push towards $2.40 a litre, Shane Oliver, AMP’s chief economist, said two or three more rate hikes would be “overkill” given the already weakened state of the economy and families’ finances.

A rate hike on Tuesday would push the cash rate to its highest level since late 2011, and a further increase at the next meeting in November would push it to 4.85% – the highest since just before the GFC, Oliver said.
Another hike to 5.1% “is going to cause major problems for households with mortgages,” he said, pointing out that debt burdens have become substantially larger over the past two decades.

“And it would be devastating for the property market. The higher you go [with the cash rate] the greater the chance you hit a tipping point, and instead of a 10% decline in home prices, you get more like a 15-20% drop.”
after newsletter promotion
Tom Devitt, senior economist at Housing Industry Australia, said the HIA’s national affordability index hit the lowest in history at the end of June.
The silver lining from falling home values is that it makes it easier for first-time buyers to get into the property market.
Devitt said he had expected affordability to improve over the second half of this year and perhaps into 2027 – but that was predicated on the RBA not pushing borrowing costs higher.
Tuesday’s anticipated rate hike, alongside the prospect of more to come, had changed the calculus.
“In this cycle we now don’t see any improvement in affordability at all,” he said.
Taylor Nugent, a senior economist at NAB, said the prospect of more interest rate hikes suggested property values would fall further and for longer than anticipated.
Beyond prices, Nugent said the fundamental issue with the housing market – too many people chasing too few homes – was evident in an ongoing lack of rental properties and climbing rents.
“Housing affordability is a challenge not just for people trying to buy, but people renting as well,” he said.

articles.title: SpaceX launches supersized Starship into orbit
articles.summary: Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built and it is meant to support NASA's Artemis moon program.

image.caption: Image: Eric Gay/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: US airspace giant SpaceX on Monday launched its Starship spacecraft into orbit for the first. The firm hopes the Starship can complete six full laps around Earth in order to prove its readiness for NASA's Artemis moon program.
"Starship is orbital," Mission Control announced to cheers. The Launch took place at Starbase, Texas.
The laps were supposed to last around 10 hours, ending with a Pacific splashdown near Chile.

Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built. It was loaded with 26 of the latest and most advanced Starlink satellites, which were released one by one, to join the 11,000 older models already providing internet service.

SpaceX began flying Starship in 2023 and the program has seen its successes and failures of successive tests. Technical challenges remain before Starship can fulfill its mandates, such as conduct commercial flights, deploy data centers in orbit or reach the Moon or the Red Planet.
This is a developing story, more details to come...

articles.title: Seoul summons Ukraine envoy over North Korean prisoner-of-war row
articles.summary: Last week Zelensky revealed Ukraine had sent two captured North Koreans to South Korea - which Seoul says was meant to be a secret.

blocks.text: South Korea has summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador after President Volodymyr Zelensky last week announced his government had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to Seoul.
Vice Foreign Minister Park Yoon-joo lodged a formal complaint with Andrii Vieshkin and expressed "strong regret" that Zelensky had revealed the transfer, which Seoul says was supposed to be a secret.
The two North Koreans, who were among thousands of soldiers supporting Russia in the Ukraine war, had earlier told local media they wanted to be sent to South Korea.
President Lee Jae Myung called the disclosure "greatly disappointing" and said the transfer was a "highly sensitive issue" impacting national security.
Ukraine's foreign ministry declined to comment when approached by the BBC.
In early 2025, Ukraine said its forces had captured two North Korean soldiers as prisoners of war in Russia's Kursk Oblast.

After more than a year of negotiations between Seoul and Kyiv, Zelensky announced they had been transferred to South Korea at the UN General Assembly last Wednesday - adding they had not been "easy to capture alive".
Seoul confirmed the news but sharply criticised Zelensky for allegedly breaking an agreement to keep the transfer a secret.

This was partly to protect the North Koreans' families, President Lee's office said in a statement, which added that Kyiv also wanted the transfer kept secret to avoid criticism that it had given up an opportunity to exchange the soldiers for Ukrainian prisoners of war.
Lee's office explained Ukraine had indicated the soldiers would be mentioned in Zelensky's address, but not the fact of their transfer.
The spat escalated when Zelensky's office responded claiming that the two countries did not have a non-disclosure agreement.
Seoul demanded Ukraine apologise for "announcing a falsehood" and said its actions had seriously damaged trust between the two nations.
Lee faced heavy criticism at home after Zelensky's disclosure. The South Korean opposition accused him of covering up the transfer to appease Pyongyang.
Lee, whose party takes a conciliatory approach to the North, has been making efforts to reopen peace talks, with little success.
Seoul has been sympathetic to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion, but has refused to break from its longstanding policy of not providing lethal weapons to any country engaged in active war.

After North Korean troops were deployed to support Russia in 2024, Kyiv stepped up pressure on South Korea to supply cutting-edge anti-air missiles to help defend Ukraine's energy infrastructure from Russian drone and missile attacks.
"When North Korea actively participates in a war in Europe, South Korea cannot remain a distant observer," said Mykhailo Podolyak, a senior adviser to Zelensky.

"The transfer of defence technologies and capabilities from Seoul to Kyiv is not just about helping Ukraine; it is about South Korea protecting its own long-term security interests by containing the expansion of an aggressive totalitarian axis."

This July, Seoul announced a $100 million assistance package to Ukraine. Lee's office said it would be an expansion of earlier assistance which was comprised of non-lethal items including helmets, personal armour and medical equipment.
Meanwhile Russia's foreign ministry has warned it would have "no choice but to retaliate" if South Korea provided Ukraine with arms, without specifying action it might take.
South Korea has long pursued cordial ties with countries opposed to the US.

Since the collapse of the Soviet Union, it has worked to deepen trade and diplomatic relations with Russia, which borders North Korea, and views both Moscow and Beijing as key partners in efforts to influence Pyongyang.
Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko

articles.title: Homecoming parties in Guelph 'worst' yet and 'impacted the entire community,' mayor says
articles.summary: Guelph Mayor Cam Guthrie says this year's off-campus homecoming parties impacted the entire community and were among the worst they've seen in terms of resources needed to respond to it. Other cities…

image.caption: This photo of the crowd at an off campus homecoming party in Guelph, Ont., on Saturday was posted to an Instagram account called Canadian Party Life. Police had to shut down traffic in the area of Chancellors Way near Stone Road Mall late Saturday afternoon after the crowd ballooned in size, spillin

blocks.text: Kitchener-Waterloo

Guelph Mayor Cam Guthrie says this year's off-campus homecoming parties impacted the entire community and were among the worst they've seen in terms of resources needed to respond to it. Other cities in Ontario have also had their share of grief in dealing with unsanctioned student parties.
Other Ontario cities also had problems with unsanctioned homecoming gatherings
The homecoming parties in Guelph, Ont., on Saturday may have been the "worst" yet, Mayor Cam Guthrie says.
Videos shared on social media show thousands of young people dressed in red, yellow, white and black, and partying on off-campus properties near Stone Road Mall.

Thousands of young people gathered in the area in the afternoon and the crowd ballooned. Some videos show items being thrown into the crowd while another shows young people climbing up the exterior walls of a building before falling into a bush.

Police closed Chancellors Way between South Ring Road West and Stone Road West on Saturday just after 5 p.m. and shared on X, formerly Twitter, that the move was "necessary to protect people's safety."
Guthrie said people in the area "are ticked" by the party and the disruption to their neighbourhood, adding, "I don't blame them.

"It's been pretty clear that it was probably the worst amount of issues that we've ever experienced in the history of homecoming parties," Guthrie told CBC K-W's The Morning Edition host Craig Norris in an interview on Monday morning.

"Not only has there been a huge amount of resources required from our own staff for the front-line staff, if you can think about waste, and transit and bylaw issues, but then our emergency services as well, police, fire and paramedics — a lot of issues there."

"It was just really a ripple effect of issues that happened at homecoming that then impacted the entire community, including neighborhoods and businesses as well that experienced a lot of property," he said.
As of 9:30 a.m. on Monday, the Guelph Police Service had not yet posted any updates to how officers responded to the party.
People treated for head injuries from thrown bottles
Guthrie said he was also told the emergency department at Guelph General Hospital was filled with people from the homecoming parties who needed medical care.

Dr. Alex Folkl, chief of emergency medicine at Guelph General Hospital, said in a statement to CBC News that the emergency department treated approximately 60 people in relation to the homecoming festivities.
People were treated for "head injuries caused by thrown bottles, lacerations and intoxication."
"Homecoming-related visits place significant pressure on critical hospital resources. This weekend, our emergency department was stretched beyond capacity," Folkl said.

"Had we also experienced an influx of seriously ill patients or even a small multi-patient trauma event, there was a real risk that we would not have been able to provide every patient with the timely level of care they required."
He also urged college and university students "to make safe, responsible choices around alcohol and substance use."
"Doing so can reduce the risk of injury and help prevent avoidable visits to the hospital."
Hard to stop the parties, mayor says
Homecoming parties in Guelph in recent years have made headlines for similar large gatherings.
But Guelph isn't alone in dealing with unsanctioned student parties.

Waterloo has become known for an unsanctioned St. Patrick's Day party that happens near Wilfrid Laurier University each year, while other cities, including London and Kingston, have grappled with homecoming celebrations that have gotten out of control.

items: London police report no major incidents as thousands attend homecoming street parties

blocks.text: On Friday, the day before homecoming, the University of Guelph issued a statement on social media reminding students to be "mindful that your actions reflect those around you."

"Remember your Gryphon values and be respectful of your neighbours and the community you became a part of when you became a UofG student. Be safe and look out for yourself and each other," the post said.
Guthrie said it's not clear how to put a stop to the parties because once they happen on private property, there's "really nothing the government can do to try to step in."

"Especially in the world of social media right now, you say you can't do that here — and even that can be challenge to even suggest that — and then in literally 10 minutes, everybody's going to know that it's just going to happen somewhere else," he said.
He said he and others appreciated the students who gathered on Sunday to pick up trash and recycling, but that doesn't mean it's OK "for things to get out of control" the day before.
"These these students and or their guests that come here, they are guests in our city and the respect has to be there for us."

Over the next few days, Guthrie said, he will be in talks with officials from the university and emergency services. While Guthrie is not seeking re-election and a new mayor will be chosen on Oct. 26 during Ontario's municipal elections, he said the conversations "can't wait a month."
CBC K-W has reached out to Guelph police and the University of Guelph for comments about the weekend's events and will update this story as more information is shared.

articles.title: PH, Slovak Republic sign deal to boost job, business opportunities
articles.summary: The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) and the Slovakian Labor Ministry signed a joint communiqué on Monday, establishing a Labor Consultation Mechanism aimed at expanding employment and business…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 10:39pm

The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) and the Slovakian Labor Ministry signed a joint communiqué on Monday, establishing a Labor Consultation Mechanism aimed at expanding employment and business opportunities between the two countries.
DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said the agreement establishes a key bilateral platform to sustain dialogue and deepen cooperation on shared labor priorities.

"This event marks not only a milestone in our bilateral labor cooperation, as mandated by the President to deepen bilateral labor relations with countries hosting OFWs, but also a concrete expression of our shared commitment to ethical recruitment, the protection of migrant workers' rights, and the promotion of inclusive growth and meaningful employment opportunities," Cacdac said in a statement.
Cacdac noted that key areas of discussion will include sharing labor market data and job opportunities, streamlining recruitment systems, and addressing the recognition of professional credentials.

Meanwhile, Slovak Ambassador to Manila Miloš Koterec expressed optimism that the partnership will foster stronger ties between the two nations across education, culture, business, and people-to-people exchanges.
"In a relatively short period of time, Filipinos have made me feel very welcome here. This openness has made my experience in the Philippines particularly special,” the Ambassador said.

“Perhaps this is one reason I see such great potential in bringing our people together more closely through education, culture, business, people-to-people contacts, and, importantly, opportunities for Filipinos and Slovaks to work and live alongside one another," he added.

Based on DMW data, approximately 12,000 Filipinos are employed across the hospitality, construction, and service sectors in Croatia, Slovenia, and Slovakia as of October 2025. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Victoria Bossong shows golden potential in Asian Games with fastest time in 800m heats
articles.summary: Victoria Bossong makes a strong case for the women's 800m gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as she posts the fastest time in the heats

blocks.text: SPEED. Victoria Bossong in action for the Philippines in the women's 800m heats in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Victoria Bossong makes a strong case for the women's 800m gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as she posts the fastest time in the heats
MANILA, Philippines – Winning an Asian Games gold medal looks like a very real possibility for Victoria Bossong.

The Filipina-American middle distance specialist posted the fastest time in the heats of the women’s 800m on Monday, September 28, at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium as she reinforced her status as one of the Philippines’ top medal bets.
Bossong clocked 2 minutes and 2.32 seconds to banner the eight-woman final on Tuesday, September 29.
China’s Li Chunhui turned in the second-best time of 2:02.35, followed by Uzbekistan’s Sabokhat Samijonova with 2:02.64.
Bossong can go significantly faster as she owns a personal best of 1:58.52, which she achieved just last June in the USA Track and Field Lone Star Grand Prix.
That mark eclipses the Asian Games record of 1:59.02 set by Kazakhstan’s Margarita Mukasheva in the 2014 edition.
Bossong, whose mother, Catalina Atienza, is from Mindoro, gained eligibility to represent the Philippines in July and is flying the national colors in a multi-sport event for the first time.
Aside from Bossong, EJ Obiena is expected to deliver for the Philippine athletics team as he looks to defend his crown in the men’s pole vault final, also on Tuesday.
The Philippines has won one athletics medal so far courtesy of John Cabang Tolentino, who clinched the bronze in the men’s 110m hurdles. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial: Guns, negotiated government contracts revealed
articles.summary: The guns were out during the 30th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. This developed after Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, Records Division chief of the Philippine National…

blocks.text: The guns were out during the 30th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

This developed after Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, Records Division chief of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office (PNP-FEO), testified that the Vice President has 22 guns under her name, while her husband, Manases Carpio, has 29 pieces of firearms.
The firearms include pistols, revolvers, rifles, and shotguns.

House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas noted that while the Civil Service Commission only issued more specific guidelines on how government employees should fill out their Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net worth, it remains to be seen if the Vice President was able to declare the value of her and her husband’s firearms under their joint SALN filing since she assumed office as Vice President on June 30, 2022.

“Whether the guns were 22, 29 or 51, it is clear from the guidelines on filing SALN that these should be declared. While the defense pointed out that the 2025 SALN guidelines should only apply to the 2026 SALN, then the respondent Vice President must be able to explain how she declared these firearms prior to the issuance of the 2025 SALN guidelines,” Luistro said in a press conference.
“If it wasn’t particularly declared as firearms, which item did they declare these personal properties in their SALN?” Luistro added.

While the prosecution was allowed to present the witness to testify on the guns under the Carpio couple’s names, some senator -judges were unsure if these guns are relevant to the prosecution’s impeachment case, specifically on allegations of unexplained wealth.
Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo, however, said he was surprised that an individual can own as many guns, saying such lax laws could result in a person raising an army to topple the government.

Ahead of Sangalang’s testimony on guns, PhilGEPS Division Chief Rendell Sopeña testified that the Davao city government led by the Vice President’s brother, Mayor Sebastian Duterte, awarded P7 million worth of government contracts to GenCorp. Industries Inc. under negotiated procurement.

Sopeña’s disclosure came after he told the Senate impeachment court last week that various government agencies awarded around P35 million worth of contracts to GenCorp. Industries during Vice President Duterte’s term, with 49 contracts awarded to the company.

The Vice President listed GenCorp. as one of her business interests in her 2024 and 2025 SALNs, but corporate records of the firm filed before the Securities and Exchange Commission did not state the Vice President’s name as one of its shareholders.

Given the Vice President’s GenCorp.’s connection, Luistro said the prosecution landed three hits, like in a tong-its card game —the Vice President owning a business, operating a business, and engaging in a conflict of interest, all in violation of the Constitutional prohibition of such acts.
Three hits means three consecutive losses in the tong-its card game, a remark that was ordered removed from the records by Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero.
Earlier in the day, the House prosecution panel withdrew its request for the Vice President to admit ownership of the bank records subpoenaed by the court.

Instead, House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list proposed a list of stipulations or agreements for the defense, which include: that the bank accounts exist; that the bank account records were produced by the banks pursuant to the subpoenas issued by the Senate impeachment court; and that the bank records are genuine and authentic copies of records maintained and produced by the subject banks.
“To be clear, the respondent has not made any claim that they are fake or fabricated. We will withdraw our request for admission if the respondent will agree to this,” Diokno said.

The Senate impeachment court gave the defense time to consider the prosecution’s new proposal, but lead counsel Sheila Sison manifested before the court that the Constitution and court decisions dating back to 1905 have always protected the respondent’s rights against self-incrimination, including compulsion to testify.
“If the Constitution prohibits compulsion for a respondent or accused to testify for himself or herself, the request for admission should likewise be prohibited here,” Sison added.
Sleeping or praying?

While the day started with a fiery legal tussle between Diokno and Sison, the mood turned a little light when Escudero called out Manila Rep. Bienvenido Abante for being apparently asleep during the proceedings.
Luistro tried to save Abante in jest by saying the Manila lawmaker, who is a pastor, was praying for the prosecution.
In a chance interview, Abante let out a laugh and said his sleepiness was due to the unexciting question by the defense panel.

Later in the hearing, Senator Panfilo Lacson also spoke on how the defense was fielding their questions, saying nitpicking on small details was hardly making a dent in the senator-judges’ appreciation of their arguments.
Unexplained wealth witnesses
The prosecution is currently presenting evidence on Article 2, which accuses the Vice President of committing an impeachable offense by accumulating unexplained wealth through the following:
· failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her SALN, including for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
· failure to divest, and instead, willfully continued all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.
Davao City Mayor Sebastian is expected to testify as a hostile witness for the prosecution either on September 29 or 30.
Other scheduled witnesses for the prosecution for October 1 to 2 include:

items: Davao City Register of Deeds IV Kathy Florence Baldonado
City of Samal Deputy Register of Deeds III Marco Pineda and
Anti-Money Laundering Council executive director Ronel Buenaventura

blocks.text: Before the day ended, the Senate impeachment court issued a stern warning to House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list over his earlier remarks against Duterte.

“The Court hereby issues a stern warning to Rep. Terry Ridon to exercise greater restraint in future public statements concerning the merits of the pending impeachment trial. This is to ensure that any decision made by senator-judges is based not on statements publicized outside the court but upon evidence and arguments presented and tested within its established parameters,” the court added.
Ridon welcomed the verdict and thanked the court for being gracious. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
articles.summary: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

image.caption: Manchester City's Premier League title wins during this time have come under greater scrutiny in light of these alleged breachesImage: Wang Lili/Xinhua/IMAGO

blocks.text: What has happened to Manchester City?

Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty on 114 of the 115 Premier League charges over alleged breaches of financial regulations. They relate to a period between 2009 to 2018 and include allegations around financial reporting, disclosure of player and manager payments, compliance with UEFA and Premier League financial rules, and cooperation with the investigation. The Premier League has yet to comment, with the news having first been reported by The Athletic.
The process started when the charges were brought in February 2023. The review was started in 2024 before the reported verdict of guilty on almost all charges arrived on September 25, 2026.
The English champions, owned in practice by the United Arab Emirates' ruling family, deny all charges and insist their case is supported by a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence."
Has this happened before?
The Premier League has long had a reputation for rampant capitalism, but it has started to enforce financial regulations that control spending in recent years.

In 2026, Chelsea were fined €11.6 million ($13.8 million) and given a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022. The club did avoid a six-point deduction though. In the recent years before, Everton and Nottingham Forest were docked Premier League points for breaking profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

City previously won, for the most part, a similar battle with UEFA. The 2023 UEFA Champions League winners were hit with a huge fine by UEFA in 2014 over a breach of the organization's FFP (Financial Fair Play) rules. Then, in February 2020, UEFA handed City a €30-million fine and banned the club from competing in the Champions League for two years for falsely inflating sponsorship revenues between 2012 and 2016. But in July of the same year, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) overturned the ban and reduced the fine to €10 million. City denied all charges and did not miss a game in Europe's premier club competition.

The key difference in City's current case to Chelsea's earlier in the year is that Chelsea self-reported and admitted guilt, which allowed them to negotiate with the Premier League over the sanction. City have stressed that they are innocent throughout.
Has something like this happened in Germany before?

German football is by no means immune to scandals or corruption. The most prominent examples are the 1971 match-fixing scandal in which players took bribes to throw matches, and the 2005 match-fixing scandal involving referee Robert Hoyzer, who confessed to fixing and betting on matches in the second division and German Cup.

The majority of financial breaches have come from clubs not being able to prove they were financially viable. Both 1860 Munich and Uerdingen are examples of this, but major systematic abuses or breaches have not happened because the structure of German football is designed to prevent it.
The 50+1 rule: What is it?
To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio
Why is something like this not possible in Germany?

Mainly because of the 50+1 rule. In place since 1999, the rule stipulates that the parent club, for example Bayern Munich, must hold at least 50% plus one vote in its spun-off professional football company – in this case, FC Bayern München Fußball AG. This ensures that the majority of voting rights always lie with the club and its members.

The rule prevents external investors from taking complete control of a club and managing it solely according to financial criteria. It is also meant to ensure a certain level of equality, as it is not possible for a club to invest disproportionately more money than other clubs thanks to its powerful investor with a controlling stake.

The vast majority of organized fans in Germany oppose the commercialization of football. The 50+1 rule makes many fans in Germany not just paying spectators but active club members who can, for example, have a say inimportant club decisions.

Critics argue that the rule puts German football clubs at a financial disadvantage. Spending in the Premier League proves that to be true, but City's reported offenses are also proof of why the league's sustainable structure matters. The Bundesliga has been approached by DW for comment.
Do these charges have an impact in Germany?

Not until the ruling and punishment are final. However, one of the main talking points is what City's success prevented other teams from claiming, whether it be prize money, Champions League places or transfer opportunities. These are compensatory claims that might be explored should the charges remain after appeals.
Reforming English football
What happens next?

Manchester City face possible points deductions, expulsion, financial penalties or the stripping of their titles. It is unclear when the decision on what the punishment will be will come, especially given that City are expected to appeal.

The outcome also has significant impacts for the Premier League. In taking on one of its biggest clubs, having successfully punished two smaller ones, they risk appearing toothless. Certainly the eyes of European football will be on them as the impact of the decision will put the integrity of the competition into focus.

It may also see more English fans call for a model like the 50+1 rule to be integrated. Some voices were raised in England after the Saudi sovereign wealth fund PIF took over Premier League club Newcastle United in 2021, and others continued during the attempted establishment of a European Super League in 2021.

articles.title: Why the latest action from India's youth-led 'cockroach' movement is targeting the election chief
articles.summary: The 'cockroach' movement has emerged as an influential force in Indian politics. Its latest campaign targets the election commission amid a wider debate over voter rolls and public trust in electoral…

image.caption: The protests, which are backed by opposition groups, mark a ​new political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra ModiImage: Abiraj Kumar Arulgnanakumar/DW

blocks.text: India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties have demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar after a newspaper investigation alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision.

According to the probe, published in The Indian Express newspaper, some key decisions linked to the so-called Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls that began last year were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.

The Indian Express said that fellow Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months to decisions concerning voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral-roll data.

blocks.caption: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Kumar 'the biggest threat to India's democracy' [FILE: October 27, 2025]Image: Jitender Gupta/ANI

blocks.text: In one of the objections, Sandhu complained that the Election Commission of India (ECI) acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal."
The allegations presented "only one part of the picture," and "differing views" were a routine "part of decision-making," the ECI said in a statement cited by local media.
'Cockroach' movement founder calls for demonstrations
Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Kumar "the biggest threat to India's democracy" and demanded his resignation.
Dipke threatened to launch nationwide protests, beginning in Mumbai on October 2, the birthday of India's founding father Mahatma Gandhi, if Kumar did not quit by Saturday.
The Saturday deadline passed without Kumar stepping down.
After Mumbai police denied permission for the planned October 2 protest, Dipke posted on X calling on supporters to submit to mass arrests rather than comply with the ban.
Supporters staged protests on Friday and pledged to continue mobilizing despite the restrictions.
Opposition parties echoed the CJP's criticism of Kumar and the Election Commission.
Pawan Khera of the main opposition Congress party said that "Gyanesh Kumar has done nothing short of treason."

"If decisions relating to the SIR were taken without the knowledge or approval of two of the three election commissioners... then those decisions and the entire SIR exercise are legally invalid," Khera said on social media.

Congress and other opposition parties have accused the ECI of colluding with India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to manipulate voter lists and win state elections in recent years, charges both the commission and the BJP have denied.
What are the demands of India's CJP movement?
The 'Cockroach' movement, which has millions of followers on social media, forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign in July following widespread student-led street protests.

The group has laid out three demands: Kumar's resignation and criminal proceedings against him, a freeze on the SIR and the suspension of all upcoming elections, and the repeal of the 2023 law on the appointment of the election commissioners of India.
India's Cockroach movement — and why it matters
Civil rights activist Amrita Johri said the CJP's decision to target the poll panel reflects wider concerns over the lack of transparency surrounding the SIR.

"There is an absence of public consultation or a clear explanation for launching the exercise, as well as the findings of the newspaper that the two election commissioners had raised repeated objections to key decisions," Johri told DW.
"Restoring public confidence will require Kumar's removal, stopping the SIR and an independent review of the millions of names excluded from the draft rolls."
From education protests to electoral politics
Political activist Sudheendra Kulkarni sees the CJP's latest campaign as that of a pressure group rather than an emerging standalone political force.

"I do not see any separate political future for the CJP. It may remain as a pressure group for some time. But as the next parliamentary election approaches, it will have to align itself with the opposition alliance," Kulkarni told DW.
Others see greater weight in the CJP's shift.
Education minister concedes to 'Cockroach' demands, resigns
Political analyst and commentator Radhika Ramaseshan said the CJP widening its focus will not weaken what it started.

"I don't think if the CJP enlarged the ambit of its concerns and built protests around [them], it would take away from the salience and power of the first issue it highlighted," Ramaseshan told DW. "Voter rights and enfranchisement is fundamental to a citizen's existence, to upholding the sanctity of the Indian constitution."
"These are not abstractions or procedural matters. They impinge on the lives of first-time voters who make up the bulk of the CJP," she added.
What happens now?
With Kumar refusing to resign, attention will now turn to the CJP's promise of street protests starting in Mumbai on October 2.

But a protest group alone cannot simply remove a CEC. Under India's constitution, the CEC can be removed only through a process requiring action by both houses of Parliament and a special majority, on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity.
"The CJP's significance would be in increasing pressure and forcing scrutiny of the ECI's functioning," former Chief Election Commissioner S Y Quraishi's told DW.
He argues that the reported unilateral decisions are the more serious issue and should be subjected to an independent legal and technical audit.

"The practical route is judicial scrutiny, not street removal. The decisions taken unilaterally by the CEC in a three-member commission could be challenged as invalid, with the Supreme Court potentially needed to intervene," he said.
"Where the commission will not act, the Supreme Court will have to step in," added Quraishi.
The CJP's latest campaign puts it directly into one of India's most contentious disputes over electoral administration.
Whether it can sustain that momentum against the Election Commission will be a very different test for a movement that is still trying to define its place in Indian politics.

articles.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
articles.summary: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW…

image.caption: A worker operates COVID-19 vaccine production equipment at BioNTech's Marburg facility, one of the sites the company is now closing after failing to find a buyer (FILE 20/01/2021)Image: BionTech/REUTERS

blocks.text: September 28, 2026
BioNTech to close German sites after sale efforts fail

blocks.caption: The biotechnology company Biontech plans to close several sites, including one at Marburg (FILE: 12/01/2021)Image: Thomas Lohnes/AFP

blocks.text: German biotech company BioNTech says it will close three sites in Germany after failing to find buyers.
The sites are in Marburg, Idar-Oberstein and Tübingen. BioNTech is also shutting down operations in Singapore.
The Mainz-based company had announced plans in May to sell the facilities as part of a restructuring of its manufacturing operations.
BioNTech said its efforts to find buyers had been unsuccessful, citing a difficult market and investment environment.
The company said it had reached agreements with its works council on additional redundancy terms for affected employees.
The three German closures affect around 1,800 employees. BioNTech had previously said its wider restructuring could affect up to 1,860 positions.

BioNTech rose to global prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic after developing an mRNA vaccine with US pharmaceutical company Pfizer. Demand for COVID vaccines has since fallen sharply, leaving the company with excess manufacturing capacity.
BioNTech is increasingly focusing its resources on its oncology pipeline and has said the restructuring could eventually generate annual savings of around €500 million ($587 million).

articles.summary: A thunderous lift off, rapid satellite deployments and a fiery ending. That's how SpaceX's 14th launch of its Starship rocket panned out today.

blocks.text: SpaceX's Starship rocket has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after orbiting the Earth for about three hours. The mission was supposed to last about 10 hours, but the SpaceX team decided to end it early. The ship deployed 26 "next generation" Starlink V3 satellites, joining the existing constellation which deliver broadband internet on Earth. SpaceX describes Starship as "the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed" and says it will eventually carry crew and cargo "to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond". articles.title: Iranian human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh wins the 2026 Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize
articles.summary: The Council of Europe awarded human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh with the Vaclav Havel human rights prize. She is a prominent advocate for the rights of women, children and political prisoners.

image.caption: Sotoudeh has been arrested repeatedly and sentenced to long prison terms. She was released on bail in May 2026Image: Everett Collection/picture alliance

blocks.text: Human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh is one of Iran's best-known human rights activists. On September 28, she was awarded the Council of Europe's Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize.

In 2026, Sotoudeh was one of three finalists for prize. The other nominees were the Iranian-American journalist and women's rights activist Masih Alinejad and the Hungarian human rights lawyer Marta Pardavi.
The Council of Europe is honoring Sotoudeh's longstanding commitment to human rights and her work, which she has carried out at considerable personal risk.
The council said Sotoudeh campaigned against compulsory hijab laws and the death penalty, "despite repeated arrests, lengthy imprisonment and great personal risk."
Who is Nasrin Sotoudeh?

Human rights lawyer Sotoudeh is committed to women's rights, the rights of political prisoners, and the abolition of the death penalty. She has represented numerous activists, journalists, members of religious minorities, and people sentenced to death.
"In moments like this, we remember past struggles, we recall our shared ideals and we think of the individuals across the globe who stand with us," Sotoudeh in a video statement from Tehran.
As early as 2012, she was awarded the European Parliament's Sakharov Prize, along with film director Jafar Panahi. At the time, she was in prison and was unable to accept the award in person.
In 2019, she had been sentenced to 33 years in prison and 148 lashes. One reason for the sentence was her work as a lawyer for women who had protested against Iran's headscarf mandate.

Even while in prison, she continued her advocacy for human rights. In 2020, Sotoudeh went on a hunger strike at Evin Prison to protest the conditions of detention and the situation of political prisoners. That same year, she was among the recipients of the Alternative Nobel Prize (Right Livelihood Award) and learned of the award while in prison.
Voice for women's rights in Iran
During Iran's nationwide "Woman, Life, Freedom" protest movement in 2022, Sotoudeh once again became a leading voice for the rights of Iranian women.
Iran uprising seen through the eyes of Iranian women

Her decades-long commitment symbolizes the enduring resistance against state restrictions and repression. She has been arrested repeatedly and sentenced to long prison terms, including in April 2026. In May, she was released on bail.

The Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize recognizes "outstanding civil society action in defense of human rights" in Europe and elsewhere. The prize is worth €60,000 and is awarded by the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) in cooperation with the Charter 77 Foundation.

articles.title: Heat pump sales soar across Europe after states cut electricity taxes, data shows
articles.summary: EU to push members to cut tax rate below duty on gas, with 10%+ surge in sales also put down to fallout from Iran war

blocks.text: Sales of residential heat pumps jumped across Europe in the first six months of the year, as the Iran war sent oil and gas prices rocketing and some countries lowered electricity taxes.
Homeowners bought 1.16m heat pumps across 12 European countries, up from 1.05m in the first half of 2025, according to the European Heat Pump Association (EHPA).

Iran’s effective closure of the strait of Hormuz, an important shipping passage, severely disrupted the flow of oil and gas shipments and sent the price of crude oil as high as $126 a barrel in late April.

Soon after the US-Israeli attacks on Iran on 28 February which unleashed the seven-month war, the European Commission published plans to encourage EU governments to lower electricity tax and to speed up the shift from fossil fuels oil and gas to renewable sources of energy.

Soaring energy prices and electricity tax changes have fuelled the growth in heat pump sales so far this year, the EHPA said, which has long argued that the popularity of the heating systems depends heavily on the price of electricity.
Rather than generating heat from burning fuel, the pumps transfer heat energy from one place to another and can be used for warming and cooling a home.

In its electrification action plan, the Commission said tax on electricity should be no higher than that on gas. Brussels hopes to amend the network charges consumers pay on their utility bills to reward flexible options such as heat pumps.

Heat pump sales have risen in European countries where electricity taxes have been cut, , the EHPA said. In Germany, a subsidy scheme has led to heat pumps being the No 1 heating tech being installed, it added.
The 12 countries covered in the data are: Austria; Belgium; Switzerland; Denmark; Finland; France; Germany; Italy; Netherlands; Norway; Portugal; and Sweden.

Paul Kenny, the EHPA director general, said: “Europe is ending its addiction to a toxic, costly drug from dodgy suppliers: gas. The sooner electricity becomes the most affordable solution, the quicker we’ll get clean.

“The fix? Dropping taxes on electricity and shifting them over to fossil fuels. The European Commission has made this clear – but now all EU governments must enact it, following in the footsteps of the Netherlands and Belgium.”
after newsletter promotion

The industry body found that taxes on electricity are often higher than on gas, which drives up the cost sharply. In the UK, electricity costs more than four times as much as gas, similar to Belgium. The only country where the ratio is higher is Romania, where electricity prices are five times as high as those for gas.

The EHPA said countries that tax electricity more than gas experience slower adoption of heat pumps and are more dependent on fossil fuels. It pointed to Belgium, where heat pump uptake remains low, although the government announced tax changes for 2026 that will cut electricity costs by 3% and raise gas costs by 3%.

Separately, a two-year study by the London-based Centre for Net Zero found that installing solar panels and a battery in a UK home saves £681 a year on average. Families’ annual bills fell by almost two-thirds (62%) after they received free solar panels and a battery, based on smart meter data used to calculate their electricity bills, in news first reported by the Times.
Great Britain recorded more new solar power installations in the first half of this year than in any six-month period since 2011, according to government figures published in July.

articles.title: Multiple generations honoured at MTV VMAs as Taylor Swift, Madonna win, Dolly Parton and Nirvana remembered
articles.summary: Taylor Swift became the most-awarded artist in VMA history, Madonna won multiple times and people paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards.

image.caption: Taylor Swift accepts the award for video of the year for The Fate of Ophelia during the MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Taylor Swift became the most-awarded artist in VMA history, Madonna won multiple times and people paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards.
Snoop Dogg hosts music video awards from Peacock Theater in L.A.
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, as she is known to do.
The pop powerhouse received the inaugural Artist Director Honors on Sunday night, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

She was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. The new award is meant to recognize artists "whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."

"I got to start making music videos and being a part of music videos 20 years ago," Swift said in her speech, adding that she's been involved in making roughly 60 music videos, 18 of which she wrote and directed.
"You, the fans, make it so much fun," she said.
She also took home the top prize of the night — video of the year — for The Fate of Ophelia, from her album The Life of a Showgirl.
Swift dedicated that award to the "ultimate showgirl," the late Dolly Parton.
"I think we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time," Swift said.
Swift debuts music video

Swift also debuted the music video for her new song, Patient Zero, during the award show. She directed the visual, which stars Colin Farrell and Dakota Johnson. Johnson and Swift portray mirror images of each other.
Patient Zero is also her first single since marrying Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden in July.
The two-hour show was broadcast live on CBS from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
Madonna opened the VMAs with her 2026 single Bring Your Love alongside collaborator Sabrina Carpenter. Later in the night, the pair won the award for best collaboration for the song.
"It's been a while since I did one of these things," Madonna joked. "So, I've prepared nothing."
When it came time for her return to the stage to accept the award for artist of the year, Madonna began with, "First of all, I would like to thank my fingers because I can always count on them."

items: Australia bans fully AI-made songs from charts after Madonna cover goes viral
Madonna's back: Queen of Pop's new dance album wins over critics

blocks.text: Returning a third time to accept for best dance, she said simply, "I came alive on the dance floor.... We're all equal on the dance floor."

If her aim was to bring the dance floor to the award show stage, Madonna did exactly that in her opening number — and then some, when Charli XCX emerged from a club bathroom to perform their reworked version of Danceteria. Around them? A trove of dancers and various famous friends, including actor Debi Mazar, Sombr and Julia Garner.
The show, which was delayed 20 minutes by a tight NFL game, wasted no time getting heart rates up.
'Now that is an icon'
Snoop Dogg, a 13-time VMA nominee and three-time winner, emerged as host shortly thereafter.
"Now that is an icon," Snoop Dogg said of Madonna, before pivoting to a joke: "She ain't a virgin no more."
Teyana Taylor then presented the first award for best pop to LISA for Dream, featuring Kentaro Sakaguchi.
"Thank you MTV for this amazing award," she said while holding back tears. "All those late-night dreams brought me here today."
It was a different scene about an hour later, when LISA returned to the stage for her hip-hop heavy hitter Sawadika, which loosely translates to "Hello" in her native Thai.
There was always going to be a big musical tribute to Dolly Parton. Kacey Musgraves paid homage to the late, great country music icon with a cover of Parton's I Will Always Love You.

Parton, whose soaring vibrato vocals, poignant songwriting and sparkling costumes defined her rise from a log cabin in the Tennessee mountains to the height of stardom and acclaim, died in Nashville of cancer in August. She was 80.
Performances arrived fast and furious: Raye delivered a medley of her throwback soul, including I Will Overcome and Where Is My Husband!
Bruno Mars slowed things down with Dance With Me. Shaboozey launched into his saloon single Cowgirl, before being joined by Gunna for some hybrid country-rap with their crossover track High Noon.
Survivor host Jeff Probst and actor Brandon Sklenar introduced a partial reenactment of GENER8ION and Yung Lean's Storm music video — which began with Lean smashing a VMA "Moon person" trophy.
Sienna Spiro belted out her Great Expectation. It was a welcome introduction to the new talent, and Spiro was named best new artist shortly thereafter.
Orville Peck introduced a tribute to George Michael, who died 10 years ago on Christmas Day.
Surviving members of Nirvana accept award
If this year's VMAs felt too pop-heavy for some viewers, that changed when the coveted Video Vanguard Award was given to Nirvana.
"They were completely original and always fearless at a time when the status quo kind of got to the point of being formulaic," Public Enemy rapper Chuck D said of the grunge greats.
The award was presented to surviving members Krist Novoselic, Dave Grohl and Pat Smear. Frontman Kurt Cobain died in 1994.
"Kurt was one of one," Novoselic said in their acceptance speech, adding that the band never imagined its sound and esthetic would resonate with so many people.
He said the music continues to endure because people are still hungry for "something real, something uncompromising" and a message that "it's just OK to come as you are."

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial: Lacson remarks on 'too technical' defense strategy
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson remarked that the defense seemed to be focusing on too "technical" or minute details, with the result being that much of it is not registering.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 9:06pm

Senator Panfilo Lacson on Monday remarked that the defense seemed to be focusing on too "technical" or minute details, perhaps in a bid to make it appear that proof beyond a reasonable doubt is required, but with the result being that much of it is not registering.

“The way probably and probably some of the non-lawyers among the senator judges, particularly my seatmate, Senator [Lito] Lapid, understand the questions posited by the defense counsel is that the objective of the cross[-examination] was to create an iota of doubt, no matter how technical and small, to create impression that the threshold of establishing guilt is beyond reasonable doubt , which I believe, is not the case in this impeachment trial,” Lacson said.
He was referring to the proof beyond reasonable doubt that is required for conviction in a criminal case, which is different from the requirements for conviction in an impeachment case.
Lacson made the manifestation after defense counsel Robert Narvasa’s cross-examination of Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS) Division Chief Rendell Sopeña.
Sopeña is a witness for Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which accuses the Vice President of accumulating unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN) including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest, and instead, willfully continued, all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.

blocks.text: Narvasa asked the PhilGeps official about the bidding process, questions which were consistently objected to by House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas since the PhilGeps is a repository of government contracts and has no mandate to oversee bidding processes.

“Let me clarify, na hindi po ito pre-judgment. Ang hangad ko lang po is baka pwede mag-adjust kayo ng inyong defense strategy kasi I can speak for myself, pagdating sa masyadong technical at ‘yung impression na nagsisilip lang ng napakaliit na butas, mukhang hindi po nag-reregister,” Lacson said.

(Let me clarify that this is not pre-judgment, My goal is that maybe you can adjust your defense strategy because when it comes to too technical issues, and the impression of just nitpicking, it doesn’t quite register.)

“A lot of good points have been raised in this trial. But we are talking among ourselves. Our observation is that parang pong hindi masyadong [nag]re-register, para bang napakaliit na butas na masyadong technical. Medyo hindi po tumatalab,” Lacson added.
(Our observation is, it’s concerns a molehill, if not too technical. It doesn’t make a dent.) — BM, GMA News
